solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greatest achievement of expert enthralling millions

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold someone captive, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A specialist's finest work is said to have captivated millions of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the highest point or peak of perfection, the very best thing anyone has done.

clue.text: War vehicle in church, leading to a disturbance

indicators.note: the church abbreviation comes first and goes on ahead of what follows in the down light

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
taken as written
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: An armoured vehicle parked in a church provokes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' looks like placing the vehicle inside the church, but it only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used by ancient armies in battle and racing.

clue.text: School said to be taken in

indicators.note: said tells us to go by how the school's name is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: Eton is a famous English boarding school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A school is rumoured to have been fooled by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like being deceived, but it means swallowed: food that has been consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has been swallowed and ingested, literally brought into the body.

clue.text: Irresponsible act of Nero, supposedly cheating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the emperor Nero is said to have played music while Rome burned
second meaning: falsifying accounts or swindling, in informal speech

explanation.walkthrough: The legend says Nero played the fiddle while Rome burned; the same word is slang for dishonest manipulation of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a violin while the city burned, and also informal slang for fraudulently tampering with accounts.

clue.text: A Parisian going after loud and amusing activities

indicators.note: going after places the French word behind the musical letter in the light

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
the French for 'a' is un

explanation.surface: A woman from Paris pursues noisy, entertaining pastimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment or light-hearted entertainment, the pleasure taken in playful pastimes.

clue.text: Turns aside from area in East Anglian town

indicators.note: in places the area word inside the name of the town

parts.note: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, in eastern England
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: Someone diverts away from a district of a small Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the region of eastern England covering Norfolk and Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone's attention is to draw it away, so the verb means turns someone's mind elsewhere.

clue.text: Somehow graceful, having smile so out of the ordinary

indicators.note: somehow suggests letters arranged in some unspecified way, a hint that they get jumbled
out of the ordinary means not in their usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A person is strangely elegant, wearing an unusually striking grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the opening adverb and 'out of the ordinary' point to rearranging 'smile so'; the definition is the single word 'graceful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a body that is supple, slender and moving with easy flexibility.

clue.text: Lord turning up in Hotel Bonaparte

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An aristocrat appears at a hotel named after the French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer or member of the aristocracy, such as a lord, holds a hereditary title.

clue.text: Seaside resort has to keep smart

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
to smart is to feel a sharp pain, as does to sting

explanation.surface: A coastal town must preserve its stylish appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings is a seaside town in East Sussex, England, famous for the battle of 1066; 'smart' looks like an adjective but is the verb for a sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a holiday town on the English south coast, an example of a resort by the sea.

clue.text: Old boy brought aboard ship cries

indicators.note: brought aboard means put inside the vessel, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
OB is short for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil carried onto a vessel is weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means weeps noisily with convulsive gasps, a verb matching the third-person form.

clue.text: European hostelry led by female

indicators.note: led by puts the female's letter at the front, ahead of the pub

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an inn is a pub or small hotel

explanation.surface: A continental pub is run by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is a person from a Nordic country of northern Europe.

clue.text: Fellow hugged by unconventional padre is forgiven

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside someone's arms, so one piece goes within the other
something unconventional departs from the normal order, so the priest's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man embraced by an unorthodox chaplain receives absolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The priest's letters are rearranged first, and the fellow then sits inside them after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be excused or let off for an offence, released from blame or punishment.

clue.text: Permit, fancy green, for traveller

parts.note: a pass is a document that permits entry

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornate, so the colour's letters are worked into a decorative new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A permit and a smart green outfit, intended for someone on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning to like green, but it signals the letters of green being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding in a vehicle who is not driving it, a person being carried on a journey.

clue.text: Hasten around capital city

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about and turned round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to hurry round the metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the seat of government of Greece, an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Demanding information in passage going out

indicators.note: in says the information word is placed inside the passage

parts.note: an exit is a way out
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone insists on details posted in a corridor as people leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the gen' is British informal for getting the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something pressing and urgent, requiring immediate attention or action.

clue.text: Make box for storing eggs primarily

indicators.note: a box for storing holds things inside it, so the selected letter goes within

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box for transport

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions to build a carton for keeping eggs in.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something into existence or produce it is the verb's meaning; both are imperative verbs.

clue.text: Garden style is supreme and surprisingly airy

parts.note: top means best or highest

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardening fashion is described as excellent and unexpectedly light and open.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of clipping hedges and shrubs into ornamental shapes is a recognised horticultural fashion.

clue.text: Company vehicle, one provided by head

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
the Roman numeral for one
a ness is a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A firm's car, one of them supplied by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the company boss, but it is a geographical headland, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial firm or enterprise is a trading organisation, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Employment of university person deemed wise

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: The hiring of an academic regarded as clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employment' suggests a job, but here it means the act of putting something to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the action of using or applying something, so employment in its sense of utilisation.

clue.text: Christian virtue of work embraced by ambassador

indicators.note: being embraced means being held within someone's arms, so the work goes inside

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title for an ambassador
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A diplomat welcomes a moral quality in someone's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith, hope and charity are the three theological virtues of Christian teaching, so it is one example.

clue.text: House was first to be susceptible to rain coming in?

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A building was the first one to let the rain in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: something punctured lets water through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with holes in it, like a leaking roof, lets weather through its punctures.

clue.text: Beware a hollow space!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Latin warning shouted by schoolchildren as a lookout
second meaning: an underground chamber in rock

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin imperative, pronounced 'kay-vee', was old British public-school slang for 'watch out, a teacher is coming'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin imperative used as a lookout's warning, and also a natural chamber in a hillside.

clue.text: Girl sitting by one slope in biblical territory

indicators.note: sitting by puts the pieces side by side in a row

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
the Roman numeral for one
to lean is to slope or tilt

explanation.surface: A young woman perches beside a single incline somewhere in the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something from Galilee, the northern region of Israel where much of the New Testament story is set.

clue.text: Cover I had left on top

indicators.note: in a down clue on top means placed above, so left comes first

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A cover I had left lying above something.
explanation.definitionFit: A removable top for a box, jar or pot is a covering, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Bothered, deep rest being tricky

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and devious, so the letters will not stay in plain order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is disturbed because a sound sleep proves elusive.
explanation.definitionFit: To be harassed or annoyed by repeated demands is to be nagged and troubled, a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Periods when shock is reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so go by the spoken form

parts.note: a daze is a stunned state brought on by a shock

explanation.surface: Times of the month when a fright gets passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of twenty-four hours are measured spans of time, plural nouns matching the definition.
